QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_30

question.text: Why does Ch 4.3(i) emphasise a 'clear withdrawal protocol' envisioned during the planning stage?

answer.text: To allow donors to withdraw pledges early
To return unused funds to the government
To terminate the project without any follow-up

To sustain project outcomes beyond the implementation period, transforming short-term outcomes into lasting impact through exit/takeover planning with stakeholders, co-commitment instruments, and institutionalised processes

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 4.3(i) and 4.3.3(iv), a withdrawal protocol (Exit/Takeover Protocol) is meant to sustain project impact beyond the implementation window. Post-midterm planning with stakeholders, co-commitment instruments, and institutionalised processes ensure assets, capacities, partnerships and networks built during the project continue to deliver impact after SE involvement ends. The Trap: A, C, B misread the protocol as funder-exit, project-termination, or fund-return mechanisms — none match the chapter's sustainability framing. Cross-Exam Context: Exit/sustainability protocol is tested in XXIII Ch 3/4 and parallels CSR project life-cycle exit under Section 135 (X-A Investment Adviser). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Request the Exit/Takeover Plan during pre-AIR fieldwork. If it is absent, the claimed 'impact' has no sustainability backbone — qualify the AIR with a scope note on post-project sustainability uncertainty.
